sources: Built from 43 web calls (19 searches, 24 page fetches) · NFL.com, AtlantaFalcons.com, Giants.com, Commanders.com, FantasyPros, Pro Football Network, DraftKings Network, DraftSharks, Sports Illustrated/OnSI, Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, RotoWire, amNewYork, BlackAndTeal, ESPN

tonight.headline: 40.8–0 with thirteen games to go, and the tight end seat is the only thing you can still change.
body: Josh Allen's 40.8 is still the only score in this matchup. Panda Attack put up nothing on Thursday because the one Thursday player they had, Dalton Kincaid, was in slot 20. ESPN projects the rest of the week at 143.5 to 125.1 and gives you 59%.

Nothing you do in the next four hours changes the lead. What it can change is who occupies your second tight end seat: Baltimore kick at 11:00 your time and Mark Andrews is a free agent until then. After 11:00 that seat is frozen for a week.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Panda Attack have two starting quarterbacks and 18/17/16 at running back on ESPN's numbers. They only need one of those backs to run away with a game script. Your own week is back-loaded in a way theirs is not: Isaiah Likely does not kick off until Monday 18:15, so this will look decided on Sunday night and will not be.

case.label: What you actually control
case.body: One roster move, before 11:00. The starting nine are set and every one of them has a live reason to be there. There is no lineup change worth a point in this league this morning, and saying that plainly is the whole answer.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore ruling Mark Andrews out on the inactive list at 11:30, or another manager taking him first — he is a free agent to all ten teams and ESPN never shows you their pending moves.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Baltimore kick 11:00 Mexico City · free agent, no priority spent
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mark Andrews
doFirst.subtitle: Fourth run carrying this card and the first with the target numbers behind it. Flowers is out, Andrews had a 25% target share in Week 1, and Pitts is behind a career backup for a second straight week.

case.label: The incoming player
case.body: Zay Flowers is out with a hamstring and Baltimore have also lost Ja'Kobi Lane to a fractured wrist. DraftKings Network's Week 2 piece puts Flowers and Mark Andrews at 25% of Baltimore's targets each in Week 1 and calls Andrews the tight end who stands first in line for the leftover work. Lamar Jackson is throwing. Andrews is 82.3% rostered nationally and a free agent in this league, which is the ownership anomaly STRATEGY section 4 ranks as the strongest single wire signal.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Kyle Pitts cannot enter Chem's RB/WR flex in any week this season, so he is a bench-only tight end behind Isaiah Likely. NFL.com, ESPN and AtlantaFalcons.com all confirmed on 18 September that Michael Penix Jr. is ruled out again and Cooper Rush gets a second straight start against Carolina. ESPN projects Pitts 10.4 anyway; that number assumes a quarterback Atlanta does not have.

case.label: Where the reporting disagrees with itself
case.body: CBS Sports ran an item headlined 'Ravens Rashod Bateman in line for No. 1 role' and quotes the club to that effect. I am not using it: that piece references Week 18 and lists Isaiah Likely as a Baltimore tight end, and Likely has been a Giant all season in this league. It is last season's article. The current reporting — DraftKings, 18 September — has Bateman at one target and a 4.2% share, last among ten Ravens pass-catchers. I take Andrews.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Baltimore ran 37 times to 25 passes in Week 1. Vacated targets in a run-heavy offence do not always reappear, and DraftKings say so in the same article that recommends the move. This is a bench upgrade on a seat that is dead either way, not a week-winner.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Andrews finishes outside the top twelve tight ends today while Pitts clears five targets — then the seat was never the problem and this churn cost a 93.3%-rostered trade chip for nothing. Or Baltimore list Andrews inactive at 11:30, which ends it before it starts. Or Rashod Bateman draws seven or more targets while Andrews draws under five, which says the vacated work went outside and the CBS read was right for the wrong reason.

doFirst.sources: DraftKings Network · NFL.com · AtlantaFalcons.com · ESPN · CBS Sports · FantasyPros

action.label: Add Mark Andrews · drop Kyle Pitts

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — do not fire this
doFirst.title: Kyle Monangai for Jaylen Warren at RB2 — unarmed for a fourth run
doFirst.subtitle: Kept on the board because today's reporting made its premise stronger, not weaker. Still not fired, because the touch count and the short-yardage work still point the other way.

case.label: The correction that matters
case.body: This brief told you for two runs that Jaylen Warren is Pittsburgh's primary passing-down back. DraftSharks' Week 1 charting says the opposite: Rico Dowdle ran 20 routes to Warren's 13 and held the third-down edge nine snaps to two, on a 58% overall snap share. Dowdle also led early downs 25-17. The passing-down claim was wrong and it is retracted here rather than quietly dropped.

case.label: Why it is still not fired
case.body: Warren out-targeted Dowdle six to two, caught five for 27, and took both of Pittsburgh's short-yardage carries. In full PPR the target count is the part that pays. DraftSharks' own conclusion is that if the split holds, neither back is trustworthy beyond a low-end RB2 — which describes Warren and Monangai equally, and a coin flip is not worth a lineup move.

case.label: The alternative
case.body: Kyle Monangai shares Chicago's backfield targets with D'Andre Swift in an offence that scored 59 points in Week 1. Chicago's Week 1 target leader was Kalif Raymond, not a back and not a tight end, which is a spread-it-around profile rather than a concentrated one.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Dowdle out-touches Warren this afternoon — that fires Warren's own clause for a second unit and opens the RB2 slot on Tuesday 22 September. Or D'Andre Swift appears on Chicago's inactive list before 17:00 UTC, which makes Monangai the lead back and makes this card live rather than ghost. If Warren out-touches Dowdle again, the snap-count read was noise and this closes WRONG.

doFirst.sources: DraftSharks · CBS Sports · Sports Illustrated/OnSI · ESPN

whatWentWrong.title: The statement that put Rashod Bateman on your watch list this morning is probably a year old
whatWentWrong.lead: It was published at 06:07 today on a CBS item quoting the Ravens making Bateman the No. 1 receiver. That item also calls Isaiah Likely a Raven and references Week 18.

case.label: What went in
case.body: The 06:07 run moved Bateman from Do-not-chase to the watch list on a club statement that he 'will move into the top receiver spot' with Flowers out. That was the right direction of travel for a real statement — a club contradicting a number beats the number.

case.label: What is wrong with it
case.body: The CBS piece carrying that quote lists Mark Andrews and Isaiah Likely together as Baltimore tight ends and describes a Week 18 game. Likely signed with the Giants and has played every snap of this season there. The article is from last season and the quote is not this week's news.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: It does not change the Andrews card — it removes the strongest argument against it. Bateman stays on the watch list rather than being deleted, because his Week 2 line will settle it either way this afternoon, but the row is now a question rather than a lead.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Baltimore source dated this week naming Bateman the top receiver. If one exists I did not find it in four searches of Ravens Week 2 coverage.

whatWentWrong.title: Your RB2 is not the passing-down back this brief told you he was
whatWentWrong.lead: Rico Dowdle held Pittsburgh's third-down snaps nine to two and ran 20 routes to Jaylen Warren's 13. That was in the Week 1 charting the whole time.

case.label: The number
case.body: DraftSharks: Dowdle 58% of snaps, 20 routes, 25-17 on early downs and 9-2 on third downs. Warren's 11.4 projection is built on a role he does not have.

case.label: What survives
case.body: Warren took six targets to Dowdle's two and both short-yardage carries. He is still the back who gets the ball near the line and the back the quarterback looks at. The role is split, not lost.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The Monangai card above stays unarmed, and Warren's thesis is now on its second recorded warning. If Dowdle out-touches him this afternoon the RB2 seat opens on Tuesday and the answer is whoever the wire looks like then.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Warren out-touches and out-targets Dowdle again today. Two weeks of that says the snap share is measuring a rotation and not a pecking order, and the correction was an overreaction.

roster.footnote: One game is played and thirteen are not, so the right column is the matchup. Nine tiles are dashed. Every one means I went looking for a published read on that defence this morning and came back without one — not that the matchup is average. Two games into the season a positional points-allowed rank is one game of data, so where reporting gave me something better than a rank it is in the detail line instead, and where it gave me nothing the tile says so. This is a 07:00 run: the official inactive lists for the 11:00 games are not out yet.

starting.name: Josh Allen
starting.detail: BUF · beat DET · banked Thursday, the second-best quarterback week of the slate

starting.name: De'Von Achane
starting.detail: MIA · at SF · SUN 14:25 · Malik Willis throwing — named Miami's starter on 8 September on a three-year deal, and NBC Sports have his toe cleared after three full practices. The carries are capped in this game; the catches are not.

starting.name: Jaylen Warren
starting.detail: PIT · at NE · SUN 11:00 · Dowdle took 58% of the snaps, 20 routes and nine of eleven third downs; Warren took six targets, five catches and both short-yardage carries. The snap count and the touch count disagree and the touch count is the one that pays.

starting.name: Terry McLaurin
starting.detail: WSH · at DAL · SUN 14:25 · Jayden Daniels throwing — he took every snap in Week 1 and is not on the report. McLaurin is not on Washington's Week 2 injury report at all; the quad clause in his thesis never tripped.

starting.name: Justin Jefferson
starting.detail: MIN · at CHI · SUN 11:00 · Carson Wentz throwing — Kyler Murray ruled out with a concussion, and Minnesota are also without Jauan Jennings, which concentrates the targets rather than thinning them.
starting.gradeEvidence: Chicago 14th of 32, 8.23 projected — FantasyPros' 'find something better' tier

starting.detail: NYJ · vs GB · SUN 11:00 · Geno Smith throwing — 19 of 24 for 215 in Week 1, his best game since November 2025. Wilson led the Jets with seven targets and 79 yards.

starting.detail: NYG · at LAR · MON 18:15 · Jaxson Dart throwing — 79.3% completions, three touchdowns, 134.2 rating in Week 1. Next Gen Stats: Likely was the first Giant since at least 2016 with two wide-open touchdown catches in one game. Your last slot to lock and the only one that survives Sunday.

starting.detail: BAL · vs NO · SUN 11:00 · New Orleans gave up five sacks in the first half of Week 1 and threw two interceptions. Required weekly comparison, answered hold: nothing free on this wire is close.

starting.name: Tyler Loop
starting.detail: BAL · vs NO · SUN 11:00 · held for a tenth straight run. Best actually available here is Chase McLaughlin at K6, then Pineiro K12, Smack K13, Santos K14. The hold is a decision, not an omission.
starting.gradeEvidence: Pro Football Network final Week 2 kickers: Loop K4

bench.name: Bhayshul Tuten
bench.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · 48% of snaps, 52% of the carries, 36% of routes; Chris Rodriguez Jr. took 41% of snaps and 40% of routes on only 21% of the carries. No goal-line work in Week 1. Liam Coen said he 'ran nasty'.

bench.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
bench.detail: ATL · vs CAR · SUN 11:00 · Cooper Rush starting for a second straight week, confirmed 18 September by NFL.com, ESPN and the club. Penix ruled out again. This is the drop on the card above.

bench.detail: CHI · vs MIN · SUN 11:00 · shares Chicago's backfield targets with D'Andre Swift. Kalif Raymond led the Bears in targets, catches and yards in Week 1, which is a spread-it-around profile. Held, not dropped, for a fourth run.

bench.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
bench.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · shoulder cleared, he plays. Benched on the matchup, not on health — Yahoo's Week 2 preview has Patrick Surtain II on him for a decent share of snaps and Riley Moss on Meyers.
bench.gradeEvidence: Yahoo Week 2 preview: Surtain II draws him

bench.name: Jalen Coker
bench.detail: CAR · at ATL · SUN 11:00 · Bryce Young throwing. SI project him 5 for 99 today and call his stock surging — with the caveat that Week 1 usage may have been inflated by Tetairoa McMillan's bad game rather than a permanent role change.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: The biggest receiver ownership anomaly on this board, and today he draws the corner who is not Surtain.

case.label: The role
case.body: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on the Chem wire, at 76.7% rostered nationally and a free agent here. Yahoo's Week 2 matchup piece has Riley Moss on Meyers while Patrick Surtain II takes Brian Thomas Jr. — the softer half of Denver's coverage.

case.label: Why not today
case.body: He is not a Do-first card because the move he would make is a swap for Brian Thomas Jr., and that swap is decided by what the two of them do this afternoon, not by what they project this morning. Claiming him now would cost a roster move to pre-empt information that arrives in six hours.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tuesday 22 September, if Meyers out-targets Thomas at Denver while Thomas is shadowed by Surtain — that is Thomas's own thesis breaking, and Meyers is the replacement. If Thomas wins the target count this row closes and Meyers comes off the list.

worthALook.name: Rashod Bateman
worthALook.lead: Demoted from this morning's lead to an open question. The quote that promoted him appears to be from last season.

case.label: What is actually known
case.body: Zay Flowers is out with a hamstring and Ja'Kobi Lane has a fractured wrist, so Baltimore are two receivers down with Lamar Jackson throwing. That part is this week's news and it is why he stays on the list at all.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: One target and a 4.2% share in Week 1 — last among ten Ravens who saw a target. DraftKings note that Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester both out-targeted him in the opener, which is not what a No. 1 receiver looks like the week before he becomes one.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Seven or more targets at New Orleans today makes Andrews the weaker half of the pair and Bateman a free claim on Tuesday, since Chem priority resets weekly and costs nothing. Under five and the vacated work went inside to Andrews, which confirms the card above and closes this row for good.

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: Structurally spent for this week. He clears after Buffalo have already played.

case.label: The timing problem
case.body: He is on waivers clearing 07:00 UTC on 23 September — Tuesday 01:00 your time. Buffalo played on Thursday. Whatever the sleeper note that surfaced him was about, it has already happened and you cannot buy it.

case.label: Why the row stays
case.body: 68.7% rostered nationally and available here is still the ownership band that matters in a ten-team league, and Chem priority resets weekly so the claim is free when it does clear.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Wednesday 23 September, if he cleared six or more targets against Detroit on Thursday. The drop is whoever of Monangai or Brian Thomas Jr. had the worse Sunday. Fewer than six targets and the note was about game script, and this row closes.

doNotChase.name: Rachaad White
doNotChase.lead: The top why=OWNED running back on this wire, and the second back in his own backfield.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Washington's Week 1 backfield snaps: Jacory Croskey-Merritt 33, Rachaad White 27, Kaytron Allen 6, out of 67 plays. RotoWire's headline on his Commanders debut is 'Quiet'. A committee back who is second in his own committee is exactly the flex body STRATEGY section 4 calls a bad add.

case.label: Why the number looks good
case.body: 164.6 season projection and 65.9% national ownership. Both are describing the job he had in Tampa, not the one he has now, and his ownership is drifting down rather than up.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Croskey-Merritt missing a game, or White clearing five targets in a week. Either turns a committee body into a role. He is also the second running back Team 13 start in IPADE, so if he is dropped or benched there, that league's Lamar offer loses its 'their gain' number.

doNotChase.sources: RotoWire · Davis Mattek snap charting · ESPN

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: 74.9% rostered, free here, and playing with the backup quarterback for a second straight week.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Kyler Murray was ruled out with a concussion and Carson Wentz starts again at Chicago. Minnesota are also without Jauan Jennings. Addison is the third mouth in that offence behind Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson, and a backup quarterback shrinks the pie before it is divided.

case.label: Why he is on the board at all
case.body: 171.4 season projection and dropped inside this league by JuiceJam on 16 September, which is the why=OWNED band. Recorded here so the anomaly does not read as a discovery next run.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wentz clearing 250 passing yards with Addison above a 20% target share, or Murray clearing the concussion protocol for Week 3. Either reopens him, and Chem priority resets weekly so he is cheap to claim at that point.

doNotChase.sources: CBS Sports · Star Tribune · Sports Illustrated/OnSI

doNotChase.name: Xavier Worthy
doNotChase.lead: 74.3% rostered nationally and free here, and the people who rank him are writing about cutting him.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 start-sit piece on him is headlined 'Close to a Cut'. Kansas City threw for 184 yards in Week 1 as a team — there is not enough volume there for a third receiver, and Rashee Rice is ahead of him and off the injury report.

case.label: The ownership trap
case.body: The 74.3% is the draft-day price, not the current one. Recorded so it does not read as a discovery next run, which is the failure mode this section exists to prevent.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Kansas City's air-yards profile normalising across two weeks, or Rashee Rice missing time. Rice is entirely off Kansas City's Week 2 injury report, so that second branch is closed for now.

doNotChase.sources: Pro Football Network · NBC Sports · ESPN

doNotChase.name: Chase McLaughlin
doNotChase.lead: The best kicker actually available to you, and still not better than the one you have.

case.label: The comparison, run every week
case.body: Pro Football Network's final Week 2 kicker board: Tyler Loop K4, Chase McLaughlin K6, Eddy Pineiro K12, Trey Smack K13, Cairo Santos K14, Evan McPherson and Chris Boswell lower. Loop is the best kicker on this roster or this wire.

case.label: Why it is reported anyway
case.body: STRATEGY section 5 requires the kicker comparison every run so that holding is a decision rather than an omission. Two ranks of difference in the wrong direction is not a move; a stream that gains nothing costs a roster slot for nothing.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop finishing outside the top twenty kickers today, or Baltimore's implied team total falling below 22 for two straight weeks. Then the seat opens and the answer is whoever tops the board that week.

settled.result: All 126 one-for-one pairings re-scored against this snapshot on both sides' optimal lineups. Zero produce a season-projection gain for both teams. Unchanged.

cannotSee.label: Nine of fourteen roster tiles are dashed and that is the honest number
cannotSee.body: Two games into the season a positional points-allowed rank is one game of data. I graded the five tiles where a published Week 2 board gave me a defence read and dashed the nine where it did not, rather than inventing a middle value. The Rams, Cowboys, Falcons, Broncos, Patriots and Minnesota defences are the ones I could not price against a position.

cannotSee.label: Search results are mixing seasons
cannotSee.body: At least one CBS item returned for a Week 2 2026 query describes Week 18 and puts Isaiah Likely on Baltimore. I caught that one because Likely's team was checkable against this file. I cannot promise I caught every one.

cannotSee.label: Season projections still look frozen
cannotSee.body: seasonProj returned figures identical to earlier snapshots. The trade search that found nothing is priced on a field that may not have moved since August, so 'no Chem trade' is a weaker statement than it reads.

cannotSee.label: The Chem trade section is empty and that is a finding
cannotSee.body: Every one-for-one pair across all nine opposing rosters was scored on both sides' optimal lineups this morning. Zero produce a gain for both sides on season projection. The six pairs that gain on this week's projection are all worth under 1.5 points and three of them give up a top-five player, which STRATEGY section 7 forbids outright.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own. Mark Andrews is a free agent to all ten managers this morning and anyone can take him before 11:00 without warning.

cannotSee.label: I did not independently confirm Kansas City's or Indianapolis' starting quarterback
cannotSee.body: Neither team has a player in your Chem lineup, so it does not touch a call here. I confirmed the starters for Miami, Minnesota, Washington, the Jets, Chicago, Carolina, Atlanta, Baltimore and the Giants, which covers every pass-catcher on this roster.

cannotSee.label: One of your starters plays Monday and one has already played
cannotSee.body: Josh Allen is banked at 40.8 and Isaiah Likely does not kick off until Monday 18:15. Your matchup will look decided on Sunday night and will not be.

cannotSee.label: Defence grades are judgement, not data, especially before week 4
cannotSee.body: The five grades here rest on a weekly streaming board and a coverage assignment, not on a season rank in points allowed to a position. Treat them as context for a projection, never as a reason to bench a starter.

cannotSee.label: This brief does not refresh
cannotSee.body: It is as old as the run that wrote it. Inactives, the Andrews availability and every kickoff today happen after this was written and none of them will update here.
